Wyvernheart (B39)

Region (English scoring-table division): Escann.

In one sentence: Form a kingdom from an Escanni adventurer company, then use wyverns, the Crimson Deluge and unrestrained magical experimentation to build a terrifying mutant mercenary army.

v2.1 personality coordinates: Expansion 94/100 | Autocracy 94/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 82/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; thematic intensity 96/100) | Pluralism 8/100. v2.1 values: Evil (11/100), with a declining trajectory. Rebuilding arms production and dealing with werewolves that threaten villagers serve the public good; however, later text explicitly treats orcs and other sapient beings as modification material, while Burnblood involves obedience brands, culling failed subjects and non-consensual experimentation. Conquest, monarchy and the status of mages are not themselves deductions; the severe deductions come from instrumentalising bodies and personhood.

Story: high | Mission-tree length: long (34 direct B39 missions) | Version checked: the local Mod supports EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: extremely high | Tedium: medium-high (mercenary upgrades, mage politics and endgame gates) | Early pressure: high as an adventurer company | Expansion: high

Brave Brothers first, kingdom later

B39 is not on the 1444 map. You begin as the Brave Brothers (B12), one of the adventurers who entered Escann after the Greentide, using the Adventurer reform and establishing themselves on the edge of the Cannwood. The offline English Wiki adds that they originated in Treunaire in the Duchy of Verne and were led by Cicera síl Treunnaire; that is setting background, while the current opening and formation rules remain governed by the Mod. B39's history template gives the formed country a feudal monarchy and a “Regent” in 1550; that is not a fixed event in every campaign. The current decision requires B12 to complete the adventurer state-building conditions, reach the required administrative technology and establish itself in the relevant Escanni area before it changes into Wyvernheart and receives its unique mission tree. The Brave Brothers prologue is not included in B39's 34 direct missions.

The country begins with understandable frontier-survival motives. Escann's old arms industry has declined, weapons must be brought in from far away, and werewolves in the Cannwood threaten ordinary families. The missions reopen forges, hunt dangerous beasts and use the Alen to obtain wealth and territory. But under the logic that whoever is strong enough deserves to rule, survival experience gradually becomes state ideology: mages gain higher status, old nobles and city privileges are pushed aside, and the weak come to be treated as usable material.

How Wyvernheart becomes Burnblood

The mission tree's real signature is not a corps of tame wyvern riders but Burnblood. Mission and event text describe mages combining the traits of werewolves, wyverns and other creatures with fleshcraft, creating, iterating and organising special mercenaries; multi-generation mercenary templates and later breeding facilities are present in the current scripts. The Floodborn mages of the Crimson Deluge form a council, while blood brands and mage towers supply this army with political and magical resources. Artificers participate in parts of the modification process, but that does not make the country primarily an artificery-industrial route: its centre of power remains mages, bloodlines and a magical army.

The story becomes darker as it advances. The text explicitly describes living experimentation, using the bodies of orcs and other people as material, obedience brands imposed on mutant mercenaries, and death as a filter for subjects deemed insufficiently perfect. It also connects hunting werewolves to the safety of villagers, so the frontier-defence public good cannot simply be denied; but the later instrumentalisation of sapient life cannot be explained away as ordinary conquest or centralisation. The personality card therefore classifies the country as evil, based on identifiable methods rather than its flag colour or imperial ambition.

What you will actually play

First establish the Brave Brothers in Escann and form B39 through the decision; then pursue military expansion, mercenary upgrades, the mage council and magical resources in parallel. The missions reach toward the Alen, the Cannwood, the north and Escann as a whole; the civil-war section and later endgame missions demand that you manage internal power and army strength. By the end, the old symbol of the “Wyvernheart” can be remade into a magical military system that dominates Escann. This is the future route supplied by the mission tree, not a kingdom or a completed atrocity that already exists in 1444.

Wyvernheart is one of the possible predecessors that can form the Black Demesne, but Black Demesne (Z99) has separate formation conditions and its own mission tree; switching changes the playstyle, and the two countries' rewards must not be added together unconditionally. Player guides often praise B39's story and unusual mercenaries, while others find the culture conversion, mercenary management and late transition into Black Demesne cumbersome. Those are version-sensitive community experiences, not a guarantee of the current script's outcome.

The offline Wiki's short kingdom page also records a conquest by Núrcestir in 1689. That is one later setting outcome, not the player's mission ending, and it does not make every B39 campaign doomed to fall. The Halann historical map's proposed foundation year remains a hypothesis, so this article does not adopt a single exact year.

Wyvernheart suits players who enjoy Escanni adventurers, dark magic, successive upgrades to special troops and a long character-driven campaign. It is a poor fit for players seeking a conventional knightly kingdom, a short relaxed campaign, or a story that avoids body modification and non-consensual experimentation.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here; suspicious percentages or script-valued effects require separate review. Raw script values are shown where appropriate.

Wyvernheart (B39) — Wyvernhearter Ideas

Set ID: B39_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B39
    }

Wyvernhearter Traditions

  • Land fire damage: +10% (fire_damage; raw value 0.10).

  • Advisor cost: -10% (advisor_cost; raw value -0.1).

1. Like a Liqueur on Fire

When the Wyvernhearters came to rule the lands of Cannwood and old Agradent, they also came to rule over the peoples who held ancient ties to dragon-worshipping Nimrithani... and as all Vernmen do, they took to the most exciting discoveries like a moth to a flame.

In the case of alcohol, this was literal, and Wyvernhearter mixologists came to utilize the old Nimrithani fire rituals with their own infusions. Combining the Sweetsting liqueur famous in Verne and various oils and spices with Nimrithani traditions, the cocktail, known as the Wyvern's Breath, is served as a shot on a plate saucer and set alight, causing a gust of flame to shoot out from the concoction like a breath of flame. A straw is then used to quickly consume the drink.

While complex and factually incorrect (as wyverns didn't breathe fire), the drink became popular amongst daring adventurers across Halann.

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

2. Pilferer of the Alen

Pushed beyond the White Walls to the poorer woodland hills of western Escann, the burgeoning Kingdom of Wyvernheart soon found wealth in their newfound role as stewards of the mighty river Alen. As with so many adventurer kingdoms, they were noble at first, guarding the river that linked Dameshead to Castonath against lurking orc and goblin marauders. But as the Age of Monsters died the Wyvernhearter kings found themselves pressed by rivals from all sides, and they turned to putting fickle and extortionate taxes on would-be merchants to ensure their survival.

Their pilferage knew no bounds, and during the 16th and 17th century as the Corinite Wars plunged Cannor proper into flame, refugees fled up the Alen to Escann where they thought wrongly that they would be safe from injustice. Instead, they found Wyvernhearter patrols with wand and musket in hand, asking for everything but the clothes off their back in exchange for 'protection'.

  • National tax modifier: +10% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.1).

3. Burnblood Mutants

"Do you hear that? Of scale and flesh bound. Fear them, son. They run on all fours yet can stand like a man. They were men, once, you know? Now warped by foul magics banned out west. They lurk the Cannwood, as if wolves, see, seeking flesh and prey like us. The wyvern-men. Don't bother running. Fight back, if you can. Bullets won't help ye, so use that bayonet of yours. Pray to Corin and avoid their great maws and their talons at all costs. If you don't, you'll be dead already, see? For their blood burns with venom off their namesake. All it takes is a drop and it'll sear you from the inside."

-Unknown Corinite refugee

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.10).

4. Anointed by the Flood

When the Crimson Deluge came, all of Escann came to know that Corin was their lady and saviour, none more so than the Kingdom of Wyvernheart. Already bound to feats of glory and bravery, the people soon came to see the Floodborn: the poor mages of Escann whose lungs would fill with foul liquids every time the Deluge struck, as bearers of Corin’s suffering and determination. Those that survived went onto to become the Witch Kings of Escann, and in Wyvernheart, became the living embodiment of the divine right of kings.

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

5. Brave Minds Think Alike

As artificery grew beyond the curated confines of the gnomish Gommo, many human artificers found themselves cast out and ridiculed for doing as humans do: pushing the limit. It is said that the first generation of immoral artificers, while few, found themselves a home in places like Corvuria and Wyvernheart. And while ordinary Corvurians were suspicious of them, as is their wont, in Wyvernheart they were treated with respect for having the bravery to push the burgeoning fields of science.

Whilst the mages created the Burnblood, it is said that the artificers of Wyvernheart perfected them... much to the chagrin of mages. By the time the magical class realized the full promise of artificery, the brave minds of Wyvernheart had already entrenched themselves with an army of mutants at their beck and call, if they so felt threatened.

  • Technology cost: -5% (technology_cost; raw value -0.05).

6. Rise of the Regent

All feared him, the most powerful war wizard in Cannor: the Regent of Wyvernheart.

As all of Escann crumbled before the might of Nurcestir, Wyvernheart stood steadfast. Even while the nobles of his own kingdom plotted and schemed against the crown and each other, the Regent of Wyvernheart kept them bound to his will through callous rule and wanton violence: the only language he saw that other magical nobles understood.

But he never did it for himself. He did it for his family. For his undying love for the last of his kin: his nephew, the timid yet magically gifted king.

Still... those who threatened the crown would come to know that a new type of wyvern flew in Escann, and the Regent would bring magedeath to entire households with a thought, entire armies with a flick of a finger, slaying the most powerful Witch Kings of the age with an extension of a wrist.

  • Leader land fire: +1 (leader_land_fire; raw value 1).

  • Land leader maneuver: +1 (leader_land_manuever; raw value 1).

7. Fall of the Regent

Of course, the Regent possessed no true friends; only enemies now and enemies later. When he broke through the White Walls and marched on Castonath, he was left without supplies and reinforcements and captured by King Camir of Núrcestir with the aid of his faithful companions Verindir and Erelorna. While he rotted in prison and Escann fell to Camiran rule, he heard word... his nephew had been slain in a bloody coup orchestrated by the nobles who sent him off to war in the first place. In 1689, after a year of imprisonment, he broke out and killed his way through the Splendid Court. But when he found Camir, he did not kill him, instead offering his service. In return, the Regent was released upon his own kingdom, and alone he wiped out the entirety of the Wyvernheart nobility, whether they were suspect in the coup or not, leaving in his wake countless ruined towns, castles and palaces all across the country.

Camir, however, was not a content man, and more importantly not a man who tolerated wild dogs without a leash. The night after his last victory, all eight of the Royal Wizards of Núrcestir descended upon the Regent of Wyvernheart and slew him... but not before five of them died at the Regent’s hands. After that peace was finally restored in Wyvernheart, and the peasantry came to know stability, albeit under Camiran yoke.

  • global_autonomy: -0.05% (global_autonomy; raw value -0.05).
